newsitem.title: USA: N.Y. regulator seizes Prudential sales materials.
newsitem.headline: N.Y. regulator seizes Prudential sales materials.

text.p: The New York insurance department said it seized marketing materials from six Prudential Insurance Co of America sales offices statewide to prevent any further document destruction by the big insurer.

Newark, N.J.-based Prudential last week was fined $1 million by a federal judge for the destruction of documents at four U.S. sales offices that could be relevant to a large class-action lawsuit against it.

Investigators from the state insurance department's frauds bureau, armed with subpoenas, collected materials from offices in New York City, Long Island, Buffalo, Rochester, Albany and Syracuse in a sweep that began Friday and ended today.
The Prudential sales managers at these locations fully cooperated with the department's frauds investigators, the department said.
Prudential was not immediately available for comment.

"The purpose of this action was to ensure that no further destruction or misappropriation of sales material used by the company occurred, and to inventory all sales material used by these agents to sell life insurance policies," acting superintendent of insurance Gregory V. Serio said.
Prudential last month admitted documents were destroyed in an office in Cambridge, Mass., and in Des Moines, Iowa.
U.S. District Court Judge Alfred Wolin also found cause for action in sales offices in Jacksonville, Fla., and Syracuse, N.Y.
The document destruction is a concern for Prudential policyholders who say they were victims of deceptive sales practices.
Policyholders must show they were misled by sales agents to receive some forms of compensation under a proposed class-action settlement of their complaints.
Under the proposed settlement, Prudential last year agreed to pay at least $410 million to as many as 10.7 million policyholders.
A hearing on the fairness of the settlement is scheduled for February 24.

In its sweep of the Prudential offices, the New York insurance department collected a variety of materials, including all sales materials approved for use by the company; all sales materials that have been used and not approved by the company; and schedules or lists of documents which the company or any of its employees have destroyed or removed from the company premises.
The insurance department said it will continue to closely monitor Prudential and its use of all marketing and sales materials.

In October, the insurance department said it was beginning an investigation into the practices of life insurance agents, starting with those Prudential agents involved in the activities uncovered by an earlier, multi-state investigation.
